name: grouped
whatItDemonstrates: A single select whose options are organized into labeled groups (Fruits and Vegetables) with separators between groups, wrapped in a Field with a custom non-native label.
stateManaged: none — no value/defaultValue/onValueChange props at all; selection state is purely internal to Select.Root
nonTrivialInteractions: Select.Root receives a nested items array ({value, items} per group) for value-to-label resolution, while the visible groups are rendered manually by mapping over the same data
Each group renders a Select.Group with a Select.GroupLabel heading, and a Select.Separator is inserted between groups (skipped after the last) via an index comparison
Field.Label uses nativeLabel={false} with render={<div />} so the label is a plain div not programmatically associated with the trigger
Select.ScrollUpArrow/Select.ScrollDownArrow overlay the list edges while the List scrolls within max-h-[var(--available-height)]

name: hero
whatItDemonstrates: A minimal single select of apple varieties with a placeholder value, a checkmark indicator on the selected item, and scroll arrows when the list overflows.
stateManaged: none — no value/defaultValue/onValueChange props at all; selection state is purely internal to Select.Root
nonTrivialInteractions: Select.Value shows the placeholder text 'Select apple' until a selection is made, dimmed via data-placeholder styling
Select.ItemIndicator renders a checkmark in a grid column beside Select.ItemText for the selected item
Select.Label renders a plain heading above the trigger (no Field wrapper in this demo)
Select.ScrollUpArrow/Select.ScrollDownArrow handle overflow while the List caps at max-h-[var(--available-height)]

name: multiple
whatItDemonstrates: A multi select of programming languages seeded with two default values whose trigger renders a custom summary of the selection (first language plus a count of the rest) via a render function.
stateManaged: uncontrolled — Select.Root with multiple and defaultValue={['javascript', 'typescript']}; no onValueChange or useState
nonTrivialInteractions: Select.Value children is a render function receiving the selected value array, rendering the first selected language plus '(+N more)' or 'Select languages' when empty
Select.Positioner uses alignItemWithTrigger={false} so the popup opens as a standard dropdown below the trigger instead of aligning the highlighted item with the trigger
Multiple items can be toggled independently, each selected item showing an ItemIndicator checkmark
No ScrollArrow parts are used; the Popup itself scrolls (overflow-y-auto capped at var(--available-height)) and item labels come from ItemText since Select.Root has no items prop

name: object-values
whatItDemonstrates: A select whose item values are objects (shipping methods) instead of strings, rendering two-line name and description content in both the trigger and the items.
stateManaged: uncontrolled — Select.Root with defaultValue={shippingMethods[0]} (an object); no onValueChange or useState
nonTrivialInteractions: Select.Item value is the whole ShippingMethod object, and itemToStringValue={(item) => item.id} supplies the string used for typeahead/keyboard matching
Select.Value children is a render function receiving the selected object to render a two-line trigger (name over duration and price)
Select.ItemText holds two spans for the two-line item layout, and Select.ItemIndicator is nudged down to align with the first line
defaultValue is pre-populated with shippingMethods[0], so the trigger shows an object value on first render
